extracted.intended_audience: upper-level undergraduate or beginning graduate students learning algebraic topology (fundamental group, van Kampen theorem)
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and hypotheses for computing π1 of spaces by decomposing them into simpler path-connected open sets and applying van Kampen's theorem (with supporting lemmas and examples). Includes algebraic description of free products and how decomposition yields presentations with relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.15 hypotheses (factor loops via cover)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a space X is the union of a collection of path-connected open sets Aα each containing the basepoint x0 ∈ X and if each intersection Aα ∩ Aβ is path-connected, then every loop in X at x0 is homotopic to a product of loops each of which is contained in a single Aα.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses compactness of I to partition the loop so each subinterval maps into a single Aα, then chooses paths gi in Ai ∩ Ai+1 from x0 to the subdivision points and assembles a product of loops each lying in a single Ai. This lemma is the basic topological criterion enabling factorization of loops for van Kampen-type arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Van Kampen surjectivity conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is the union of path-connected open sets Aα each containing the basepoint x0 ∈ X and if each intersection Aα ∩ Aβ is path-connected, then the natural homomorphism Φ: *α π1(Aα) → π1(X) is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surjectivity follows from Lemma 1.15: every loop in X can be written (up to homotopy) as a product of loops each lying in some Aα, hence comes from the free product. Ensure the cover consists of path-connected open sets containing the basepoint and pairwise intersections are path-connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Van Kampen kernel description (additional triple-intersection hypothesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If in addition each intersection Aα ∩ Aβ ∩ Aγ is path-connected, then the kernel of Φ: *α π1(Aα) → π1(X) is the normal subgroup N generated by all elements of the form iαβ(ω) iβα(ω)^{-1} for ω ∈ π1(Aα ∩ Aβ), and hence π1(X) ≈ *α π1(Aα) / N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To identify the kernel one must be able to move loop-factors between the groups using intersections; triple-intersection path-connectedness is used in the uniqueness-of-factorizations argument. Without the triple-intersection hypothesis the stated description of the kernel can fail (see examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of path-connected intersections (counterexamples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intersections Aα ∩ Aβ must be path-connected (and triple intersections when asserting the kernel description), otherwise surjectivity or kernel identification can fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: covering S1 by two open arcs (non-path-connected intersection) shows Φ need not be surjective. The suspension of three points with a three-set cover with non-path-connected triple intersection shows the kernel description (or resulting quotient) can give the wrong abelianization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization and equivalence moves (algebraic description used in proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: A factorization of [f] ∈ π1(X) is a formal product [f1] ··· [fk] where each fi is a loop in some Aα and f is homotopic to f1 ··· fk. Two factorizations are equivalent if they are related by combining adjacent terms that lie in the same π1(Aα) or by regarding a term lying in an intersection as an element of either group's π1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equivalence moves correspond to reduction moves in the free-product algebra and to the relations generating the kernel N; the uniqueness (up to equivalence) of factorization is the crux of the kernel-identification argument in van Kampen's theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.19 (change-of-basepoint for homotopies not fixing basepoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕt : X → Y is a homotopy and h is the path ϕt(x0) formed by the images of a basepoint x0 ∈ X, then ϕ0* = βh ϕ1* (change-of-basepoint conjugation appears when homotopy does not fix the basepoint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs partial paths ht and assembles ht (ϕt f) ht^{-1} to get the relation. Use this formula whenever homotopies move basepoints: induced maps differ by conjugation by the track of the basepoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy-invariance under basepoint-preserving homotopies
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕt : (X, x0) → (Y, y0) is a basepoint-preserving homotopy, then ϕ0* = ϕ1*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the homotopy fixes the basepoint for all t, no change-of-basepoint conjugation occurs; induced maps on π1 agree exactly. This is the basic invariance used throughout fundamental-group arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.17 (retractions and deformation retracts effect on π1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a space X retracts onto a subspace A, then the homomorphism i*: π1(A,x0) → π1(X,x0) induced by inclusion is injective. If A is a deformation retract of X, then i* is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If r: X→A is a retraction then r i = id implies r* i* = id so i* injective. If rt is a deformation retraction then composition with rt deforms any loop in X into A, giving surjectivity as well. Use this to identify fundamental groups when deformation retracts are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.18 (homotopy equivalence induces π1 isomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ : X → Y is a homotopy equivalence, then the induced homomorphism ϕ* : π1(X, x0) → π1(Y, ϕ(x0)) is an isomorphism for all x0 ∈ X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a homotopy inverse ψ and Lemma 1.19: ψ* ϕ* is conjugate to the identity map hence an isomorphism, implying ϕ* is injective and, by symmetric reasoning, surjective. Basepoint issues are handled by the conjugation lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy: find deformation retract to compute π1
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, identify a deformation retract of a complicated space X onto a simpler subspace (e.g., wedge of circles, mapping cylinder, torus minus knot neighbourhood) and compute π1 of the retract instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: R3 − A (complement of a circle) deformation retracts onto S1 ∨ S2 giving π1 ≈ Z; complements of two unlinked circles retract onto S1∨S1∨S2∨S2 giving π1 ≈ Z * Z. Construct explicit deformation retractions or small neighborhoods that deformation retract to the simpler complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedge-sum criterion for van Kampen application
rubrics_metrics.description: If each basepoint xα of spaces Xα is a deformation retract of an open neighborhood Uα in Xα, then Xα is a deformation retract of an open neighborhood Aα in the wedge W = ∨α Xα, intersections of Aα's deformation retract to a point, and van Kampen applies to give π1(W) ≈ *α π1(Xα).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the standard sufficient conditions to conclude the fundamental group of a wedge sum is the free product of the fundamental groups of the summands. In particular, ∨copies of S1 has free fundamental group with one Z per circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free product construction and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The free product *α Gα consists of reduced words g1···gm with gi ∈ Gαi and adjacent letters from distinct factors; multiplication is concatenation followed by reduction; each factor Gα injects into the free product and any collection of homomorphisms ϕα: Gα→H extends uniquely to ϕ: *α Gα → H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand reduced-word rules (combine adjacent letters from same factor and cancel identities), associativity proof via left-multiplication permutations Lg, uniqueness of reduced forms, and the universal property which is crucial when passing from factor groups to the whole π1(X) under van Kampen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case two-set van Kampen application
rubrics_metrics.description: When X = A ∪ B with A, B path-connected open containing the basepoint and A ∩ B path-connected, the map π1(A) * π1(B) → π1(X) is surjective and the kernel is the normal subgroup generated by i_{AB}(ω) i_{BA}(ω)^{-1} (triple-intersection hypothesis is irrelevant here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This two-set situation is the most commonly used form of van Kampen. Verify A ∩ B is path-connected and compute how loops in the intersection map into the two factors to write down relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical technique: decompose knot complements to mapping cylinders
rubrics_metrics.description: To compute π1 of knot complements (e.g., torus knots Km,n) use decomposition of S3 − K into two mapping-cylinder-like pieces (Xm and Xn) whose intersection is a circle; van Kampen then yields a presentation with generators a,b and single relation a^m = b^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace R3 by S3 via one-point compactification (van Kampen preserves π1 when adding a simply-connected complement). Identify deformation retractions of the two complementary solid tori onto mapping cylinders; compute how the generator of the intersection maps to powers in each factor to obtain the relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of change-of-basepoint homomorphisms β_h
rubrics_metrics.description: The change-of-basepoint homomorphism β_h (conjugation by the homotopy class of a path h from x0 to x1) appears whenever induced maps are compared for different basepoints; σ: π1(X,x0) → π1(X,x1) depends only on the homotopy class of h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: β_h is used repeatedly: to relate induced maps coming from homotopies that do not fix basepoints (Lemma 1.19), and in proofs that homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms on π1 for arbitrary basepoints. Exercise: show β_h depends only on homotopy class of h.
